meanings: verb: combine into one
examples: The two cities of Buda and Pest were separate for centuries, but in the nineteenth century they fused to become Budapest.

meanings: verb: to gently persuade or influence to do something
examples: The kittens were shy and distrustful; even a big piece of fish on the floor couldn't coax them out from their hiding place behind the couch.

meanings: verb: to show contrast by placing two things next to each other
examples: My car is still new, but it looks cheap in this parking lot, juxtaposed with so many luxury cars.

meanings: adjective: dry, without rain
examples: Due to years of little rainfall in California, lakes are dry, rivers are empty, and forests are arid.

meanings: noun: the time when an event will happen very soon (as "on the verge of")
examples: I was on the verge of throwing my unresponsive computer out the window when I realized the battery was simply dead.

meanings: verb: dry out and die (used for plants)
examples: After two weeks on vacation, the family returned to find that their plants had withered from sitting in the sun and not receiving enough water.

meanings: verb: to move around in search for food
examples: Raccoons are experts at foraging for food: they can find scraps at a campground, under the seats at a ball stadium, or anywhere humans create trash.

meanings: adjective: angered at something unjust or wrong
examples: Geoffrey was indignant after the same driver got in front of him then slowed down for the third time.

meanings: verb: to send (a person) away permanently in punishment
examples: When my parents banished my boyfriend Mitchell from our house, he wasn't even allowed on the front lawn: he had to stay as far away as possible.

meanings: adjective: very weak
examples: After months of being sick in bed, Harry did not have all of his energy back and felt quite feeble when trying to do even simple things.

meanings: adjective: difficult to find, catch, or achieve
examples: Many birdwatchers enjoy tracking highly elusive species because the reward of actually seeing a rare bird is so great.

meanings: verb: experience a difficult change or process
examples: Aiko's school had undergone a quick but detailed renovation, making it disturbingly unfamiliar to her when she returned after only a few weeks away.

meanings: verb: to cut off from a whole
examples: With one strong swing of a heavy axe, the head of the fallen king was severed, and the people were free.

meanings: adjective: making success more difficult
examples: They were planning on pouring concrete for the building's foundation this week, but due to the rain, the conditions are too adverse to do so.

meanings: noun: a long time with not enough rain
examples: The drought left the landscape dry and lifeless; it had not rained in months, and even the river that the town depended on for water had dried up.

meanings: adjective: heavily decorated in small detail
examples: The statues on the church wall are highly ornate: it took the artist years to carve the tiny details.

meanings: adjective: important immediately
examples: It was six in the morning and she still hadn't finished the essay that was due at eight; but after working all night, her most pressing need was a cup of coffee.

meanings: verb: lift up
examples: With his face red and his teeth clenched tight, the bodybuilder successfully hoisted the weights over his chest.

meanings: adjective: attractive and old-fashioned (used especially for places or traditions)
examples: As Mary walked through the quaint little village with old-fashioned cottages and stone streets, she felt that she had gone back in time.

meanings: noun: writing made of normal sentences, not a poem
examples: Don Quixote is often called "the first modern novel" in European literature, largely because it was one of the first stories written in prose.

meanings: verb: to flow slowly through something with many small holes
examples: Some people are worried that new methods of natural gas extraction from the earth cause toxic chemicals to seep into the water underground.

meanings: adjective: dark or cloudy and hard to see through
examples: The dirt and debris from the landslide went down the river and turned the previously clear lake a murky brown.

meanings: adjective: cold-feeling and dark; hopeless
examples: Veronica bought two plane tickets to the sunny Caribbean because she didn't want to suffer through another winter in her bleak hometown.

meanings: adjective: producing many things
examples: Schubert was the most prolific composer, producing hundreds of hours of music before he died at the age of 31.

meanings: noun: a state of danger
examples: Tony Stark, the arrogant billionaire, placed the lives of his loved ones in jeopardy when he publicly announced that he was the superhero, Ironman.

meanings: adjective: extremely small
examples: Unfortunately for her students, the professor noticed even the most minute mistakes in essays that she graded.

meanings: adjective: dishonest or not giving the whole truth
examples: The public could not trust their disingenuous leader, as he was infamous for avoiding direct answers to question in every interview.

meanings: noun: the time when a big change started or arrived
examples: The advent of the Internet was a major event in human history—never before could people search for and find information so easily.

meanings: adjective: often changing suddenly and unpredictably
examples: The wild, sudden turns of the car led the police officer to investigate; when asked about his erratic driving, the driver had no explanation.

meanings: adjective: logical and understandable, without errors
examples: After several months of careful investigation, the committee decided that its conclusions were clear and sound enough to report to the public.

meanings: noun: housing that someone is living in
examples: Expecting her lazy boyfriend’s dwelling to be messy, Jane was shocked to find that the apartment was neat and clean.

meanings: adjective: showing the truth (used for a story or piece of information)
examples: When I asked William if he still loved me, he didn't say "no," but his silence was telling.

meanings: adjective: skilled in a specific ability
examples: After many years of practice and repetition, the sculptor was adept at carving perfect representations of the human body in stone.

meanings: adjective: cautious, not trusting
examples: Years of being stuck in the loud and crowded shelter made the dog wary of other animals.

meanings: verb: to persuade somebody or an animal come somewhere by promising a reward
examples: In order to lure the mouse into the trap, Gary placed a small amount of peanut butter inside.

meanings: adjective: not done well and done quickly without planning
examples: As there were no building materials readily available after the storm, victims built haphazard shelters from whatever they could find.

meanings: adjective: not harmful
examples: I thought Jim's comment about how much salt I'd put on my food were innocuous until I realized he was criticizing my health choices.

meanings: adjective: of the highest importance
examples: Although we want the mission to send a man to Mars to succeed, the lives and safety of the astronauts are paramount.

meanings: adjective: too colorful and overly decorated
examples: Karen knew the bright pink, skin-tight suit was gaudy, but she had promised her five-year old son that he could pick her clothing for the party.

meanings: verb: to add decoration and detail to make more beautiful
examples: Late last night, somebody painted cat faces on all the statues that adorn our town's government buildings.

meanings: noun: an extremely heavy rain
examples: The torrent of rain that accompanied the typhoon dumped several metres of water on the city over the course of the week.

meanings: verb: use all of (used especially for natural resources)
examples: The soldiers had carelessly depleted all of their resources, during the summer, leaving little food for the oncoming winter.

meanings: adjective: careful not to do things that hurt or anger other people
examples: Arriving in a new country can be difficult for even the most tactful person; customs that are ordinary in one country may be offensive in others.

meanings: noun: a traditional story that teaches a lesson
examples: Grandma's fables always had very specific lessons; my favorites were "The elf that always left the toilet seat up" and "the fairy that chatted on Facebook instead of getting Granny a glass of water."

meanings: verb: to manage a difficult situation, especially emotionally
examples: If we could teach children how to cope with difficult situations, they might have better emotional stability throughout their lives.

meanings: verb: to save something from the destruction of everything around it
examples: In order to keep costs down in repairing his car, Stephen salvaged old parts from a local junkyard.

meanings: noun: objects for sale
examples: The store owner was tired of shouting out onto the street all of the different items in her store, so she made wood signs listing her wares instead.

meanings: adjective: far away
examples: McMurdo station, an American research facility in Antarctica, is one of the world's most remote settlements.

meanings: verb: to turn away from or prevent
examples: After heavy rain this winter, water was released from Lake Shasta to avert flooding.

meanings: verb: to use government authority to demand payment
examples: In an effort to grow his support among the rich, the newly crowned king put an end to taxes that his father had previously levied on merchants.
